answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol isolates malicious nodes onto an untrusted island, requiring non-refundable cryptographic stake burning for identity creation. By enforcing a superlinear cost curve where minting n identities demands burning O(n^2) stake, an attacker attempting to flood our digital garden faces exponential economic friction. Rather than shifting stakes like wind across a barren dune, this burning forces unsustainable attacker deficit.
